key_insight: GenFish ranks potential protein targets for molecules using generative retrieval without explicitly treating unmeasured molecule–protein pairs as negatives.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support target discovery and drug repurposing, including oncology research, but the abstract reports no cancer-specific or clinical validation.
method: Encode frozen protein language-model features as shared semantic identifiers using residual vector quantization.
Predict identifier sequences autoregressively from a molecular fingerprint.
evidence_signal: On ProTargetBench, covering 20,431 reviewed human proteins, GenFish achieved higher mean performance across all three full-catalogue retrieval metrics than seven baselines on 198 held-out molecules.
watch_item: Recovery of recorded associations does not establish new biological targets; predictions require experimental validation.
paper_title: Generative Retrieval for Reverse Target Fishing with a Proteome-Scale Benchmark
